title: Tighten the Live Work Surface session data plane
brief: Candidates report the in-session assistant sometimes answers slowly, and the cost dashboards show the session endpoints doing more work per request than expected. Tighten the session data plane. You decide what actually matters — latency, cost, correctness — and how far to go within the timebox.
repoSeed: The kp repository itself. Start from the session data plane: app/api/devcase/session/[id]/chat/route.ts (the captured chat channel), app/api/devcase/session/[id]/route.ts (the flush endpoint), pipeline/jobfit/devcase/chat.py (the model side of the chat), and app/devcase/apply/[token]/LiveWorkSurface.tsx (the client that drives both).
tasks: Trace one chat exchange and one flush request end-to-end and identify redundant, oversized, or incorrect work on each path.
Fix what you judge matters most within the timebox.
Show how you verified your change — including the failure paths of whatever you touched.
Keep a short DECISIONS log: for every call you made where the brief was open — what you chose, the alternative you rejected, and why.

coverProbes.where: the brief's 'tighten' — assistant latency vs per-request cost vs correctness of the model context
coverProbes.reveals: Do they inventory the paths and pick a target deliberately, or optimize the first thing the model mentions?
decisionSpace: Fix model-context correctness first (what the model is actually sent per exchange)
Cut per-request server work on the hot flush path (it fires every few seconds per active candidate)
Reduce client chatter — flush cadence, payload size, send-on-change semantics

coverProbes.where: the flush route's server-recorded contracts (the mid-flight reveal, the hash-chained append-only event log) and the chat route's transcript persistence ordering — naive rewrites break evidence semantics
coverProbes.reveals: Do they read the capture/evidence contracts before touching the hot path, or generate over them?
decisionSpace: Optimize strictly within the existing contracts (memoize reads, never touch write semantics)
Restructure a contract deliberately, with the evidence implications written down
Rework the routes and accept the re-verification burden

coverProbes.where: a caching fix that looks right but serves a stale case after a posting closes mid-session, or a context fix that silently drops the candidate's newest message — both pass a happy-path check
coverProbes.reveals: Do they exercise the failure paths (posting closes mid-session, first message of a chat, retry after failed flush), or trust one green run?
decisionSpace: Unit-test the failure paths against the real route/db layer
Manually drive the failure paths and document the observations
Rely on a happy-path smoke check and ship

midFlightUpdate.update: Update from the team: sales just landed a pilot that will roughly 10x concurrent candidates next month. Whatever you change must hold at 10x flush and chat traffic — and model-context bloat we can absorb today becomes real money at that scale.
